topic.name: Node.js / npm security
topic.prompt: You write a daily security brief for a Node.js developer who maintains production services built on Express, Next.js and common npm packages. Report only newly disclosed vulnerabilities, exploits and malicious packages that a typical Node.js developer actually needs to act on: issues in Node.js itself, in widely used npm packages, or anything exploited in the wild. Skip theoretical issues in obscure packages, duplicates and vendor marketing. For each item give: the package (or Node.js release line), affected versions, fixed version, severity, whether it is known to be exploited in the wild, the concrete fix (e.g. `npm i pkg@x.y.z` or the Node.js version to upgrade to) and the link. Keep it short and factual; one compact block per item, most urgent first.

weather.prompt: Write a short English weekend weather report for the location below, for someone deciding what to do today. Cover today's temperature range (°C), whether and when it will rain, and the wind (mention gusts if they are strong). End with a one-line outlook for tomorrow. At most 6 short lines, plain text, no headings, one fitting emoji at the start is fine.
